STAGE 2 (implementation) of a 4-stage pipeline. Repo /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui. Stage 1 PROVED every claim below by execution — implement and prove the fix, don't re-litigate the problem.

FILE OWNERSHIP — you may modify ONLY these files. Two sibling agents work concurrently on `theme/components/{recipeGuards.test.ts,zimmTextInput.ts,zimmLogo.ts,index.ts}` and `ui-kits/atoms/{zimmIcon,zimmLogo}` — do not touch those.
  overrides/app/theme/components/footer.ts
  overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx
  overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.tsx
  overrides/app/types/contentful.ts
  overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeModal.test.tsx     (NEW — you create it, for S5)

DO NOT COMMIT. DO NOT `git add`.
FORBIDDEN: `npm start`, `npm run build-storybook`, `npx test-storybook` (Stage 3/4 own those). Allowed: `npx vitest run`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx tsx -e`, `npx eslint`, `npx prettier`, node, git reads, Playwright via node_modules/playwright-core against the RUNNING dev server at http://localhost:3000 (read-only page loads, for measurement).

=== M2 — two unjustified casts doing hidden non-null assertions (PROVEN) ===
`index.stories.tsx` ~181-182:
  const footer = canvasElement.querySelector('footer[role="contentinfo"]') as HTMLElement;
  const slot = footer.querySelector('[aria-live]') as HTMLElement;
Stage 1 proved: no justifying comment (typescript.md requires one for `as`); the only work they do is null-suppression (removing them yields exactly three `possibly null` errors and ZERO missing-member errors); and `HTMLElement` is a NARROWING (not a widening, as I earlier said) that buys nothing because `getBoundingClientRect` is declared on `Element`. Severity is DIAGNOSTIC QUALITY, not a false green — it throws either way.
IMPLEMENT Stage 1's recommended variant: drop both casts, keep the type as `Element`, and add two explicit guards that throw a NAMED error, e.g.
  if (!footer) throw new Error('SubscribePlaceholder: footer[role="contentinfo"] not found');
PROVE: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

=== S2 — the height assertion passes vacuously on a collapsed container (PROVEN) ===
Same file, ~203-204: a pure before/after equality with nothing constraining either operand. Stage 1 proved in a real browser that three collapse modes (`display:none`, `height:0;overflow:hidden`, `html{display:none}`) all pass vacuously — and that in jsdom every rect is 0, so the whole assertion would be unconditionally true if these stories are ever run via portable-stories/composeStories.
IMPLEMENT: add the non-zero preconditions before the comparisons:
  await expect(slotBefore).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  await expect(heightBefore).toBeGreaterThan(0);

=== S5 — the Tab trap and body-scroll lock have zero coverage (PROVEN) ===
`overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeModal.ts`: lines 79-94 (the Tab trap: FOCUSABLE query, `disabled` filter, first/last, both wrap directions) and 63-70 (body-scroll lock save/restore) have NO coverage anywhere in the repo. Covered already: mount, focus-into-first-field, Escape, focus-restore — all asserted by `SubscribeModalOpen`.
Stage 1 PROVED a `play` CAN assert a Tab trap: user-event dispatches a cancelable bubbling keydown, reaches the hook's document-level listener, and because the listener calls preventDefault, user-event SKIPS its own focus move — so the trap's `focus()` is the only one observed. Mutation-tested against a no-trap control (unwrapped forward Tab lands on `<body>`; unwrapped Shift+Tab lands on the outside trigger).
ONE CAVEAT Stage 1 found: nothing in `SubscribeModal` is ever `disabled`, so line 82's `!el.hasAttribute('disabled')` filter is UNREACHABLE from a footer story. Stage 1 recommends this split, which you should follow:
  (a) In `index.stories.tsx` — extend the existing `SubscribeModalOpen` play (or add one story) to assert BOTH wrap directions and the body-scroll lock (`document.body.style.overflow` is directly assertable: 'hidden' while open, restored after close).
  (b) In a NEW `overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeModal.test.tsx` — a Vitest test with a SYNTHETIC disabled control proving the `disabled` filter excludes it from the trap cycle.
PROVE both. For (b) you can run vitest directly. For (a) you cannot run test-storybook — so ALSO write a temporary throwaway Vitest probe that mounts the real hook and drives it with userEvent to prove your play's assertions are sound, then delete the probe and report that you did this.
CRITICAL: mutation-test your new assertions. Temporarily break the trap (e.g. make the keydown handler return early) and the scroll lock (remove the overflow write) and show each new assertion FAILS. An assertion that cannot fail is worse than none.

=== S6 — three CMS array types should be readonly (PROVEN) ===
`overrides/app/types/contentful.ts` ~104/125/126: `links: FooterNavLinkEntry[]`, `navGroups: FooterNavGroupEntry[]`, `legalLinks?: FooterNavLinkEntry[]`. Stage 1 proved: the footer only ever `.map`s them (exhaustive mutation-method grep across overrides/ found none); `FOOTER_FIXTURE` is a plain module singleton consumed by the PRODUCTION container, and a probe doing `navGroups.push`, index-assign, `.sort()`, `.length = 0` compiles TODAY; and applying `readonly ... : ReadonlyArray<...>` to a full isolated copy of overrides/ compiles at exit 0 with NOTHING breaking, while rejecting all 7 mutation vectors.
IMPLEMENT: `readonly links: ReadonlyArray<FooterNavLinkEntry>` etc. on all three. Both modifiers pull weight — `ReadonlyArray` blocks push/index/sort/length, the `readonly` property modifier additionally blocks whole-array reassignment.
Consistency note worth putting in the code: `footer/index.tsx:356`'s `BottomBarProps.legalLinks` ALREADY uses `ReadonlyArray<>`, so this aligns the entry types with the component's existing house style.
PROVE: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, and a temporary probe (deleted after) showing a mutation attempt is now rejected.

=== S7 — one story imports from an undeclared transitive package (PROVEN) ===
`index.stories.tsx:2` imports `Meta`/`StoryObj` from `@storybook/react`, which is in NEITHER dependencies nor devDependencies — only a transitive child of `@storybook/react-webpack5`. The other 11 stories use `@storybook/react-webpack5`. Stage 1 proved they are the SAME declarations (`@storybook/react-webpack5/dist/index.d.ts` line 1 is `export * from '@storybook/react'`), that it is purely type-level (`import type` + isolatedModules → fully erased, zero runtime footprint), and that switching compiles at exit 0. The residual risk is resolution-only: it works today solely because npm hoisted the transitive dep, and a pnpm/nested install would break `tsc` on this one file.
IMPLEMENT: change the import to `@storybook/react-webpack5`. One word. No package.json change (Hard Rule #7 — do not add or remove packages).

=== S10 — call-site style composition, ×3 (PROVEN — and my first proposed fix was WRONG) ===
Sites: `footer/index.tsx` 459-462 and 477-480 (identical `...(showContactChannels ? {paddingLeft:'2xs'} : {})` spreads — verbatim duplication, `grep -c` returns 2) and 497 (`sx={label.includes(NBSP) ? {width:'min-content'} : undefined}`).

TWO CORRECTIONS to what I originally proposed, both proven by Stage 1:
1. The contact column has THREE cases, not two. Line ~507's icon-row `<li>` sits inside a `showContactChannels` group but deliberately gets **0px** (measured; matches its code comment "The icon row below needs no indent"). So `linkListItem` needs a SIBLING indented part, not a replacement — the icon-row `<li>` must keep the plain part.
2. `ZimmNavItem` has NO `variant` prop — it derives `variant = inverse ? 'inverse' : 'light'` internally, so the single variant slot is already taken and a `min-content` variant would COLLIDE. Do NOT change ZimmNavItem's public API. Stage 1 proved a better fix by execution: put `width: min-content` on the `<li>` instead —
     baseline (sx on nav item)      → nav 115px, li 115px
     sx removed                     → nav 160px, li 160px  (collapses to the 160px linkCol cap)
     width:min-content on the <li>  → nav 115px, li 115px  ✅ IDENTICAL

IMPLEMENT in `footer.ts`: one shared `const CONTACT_INDENT = { paddingLeft: '2xs' }` (kills the DRY violation) plus three new parts — `columnHeadingContact`, `linkListItemContact` (each spreading its base part + CONTACT_INDENT) and `linkListItemHug` (base + `width: 'min-content'`). Register all three in BOTH the `parts` array AND `baseStyle`. Then the three call sites in `index.tsx` become part SELECTIONS (`__css={cond ? styles.a : styles.b}`), with the conditions staying at the call site — a predicate is fine there, a style value is not.
WARNING from Stage 1: `recipeGuards.test.ts` does NOT assert parts/baseStyle parity, so nothing will catch a `parts`-array omission. Verify parity AT RUNTIME yourself (`npx tsx -e` importing ZimmFooter and comparing `parts` against `Object.keys(baseStyle)`) — a static regex on footer.ts gives a WRONG answer, I made that mistake twice. Current parity is 35/35; after your change it should be 38/38.

BASELINES TO PRESERVE (Stage 1 measured, identical at 1440 and 390):
  Contact columnHeading paddingLeft            4px
  Contact link <li> × 3                        4px
  Contact <li> holding ContactIconRow          0px   ← the third case
  About / Help heading + all items             0px
  'Acknowledgement of Country' nav item + li   115 × 38 px
PROVE by measuring against the dev server after your change and showing every one of those is unchanged.

FINISH BY REPORTING: per item — what changed, the proof it works, the proof nothing moved, and for S5 the mutation-test results. Run `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest run`, `npx eslint` and `npx prettier --check` on your files, and the runtime parts/baseStyle parity check. Do NOT commit. End with `git status --porcelain`.

All six items implemented and proven. Nothing committed, nothing staged.

## M2 — unjustified casts
`index.stories.tsx` `SubscribePlaceholder`: both `as HTMLElement` casts dropped, type stays `Element`, replaced by two guards that throw named errors (`'SubscribePlaceholder: footer[role="contentinfo"] not found'` / `'…subscribe [aria-live] slot not found'`). Comment records why the cast bought nothing (`getBoundingClientRect` is declared on `Element`).
**Proof:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

## S2 — vacuous height assertion
Added before the comparisons:
```ts
await expect(slotBefore).toBeGreaterThan(0);
await expect(heightBefore).toBeGreaterThan(0);
```
with a comment naming the three collapse modes and the jsdom-all-zeros case.

## S5 — Tab trap + scroll lock coverage
**(a) `SubscribeModalOpen` play extended** with the scroll lock (`overflowBefore` captured, asserted `not.toBe('hidden')` as a non-vacuity precondition — the S2 lesson applied — then `'hidden'` while open, then restored to `overflowBefore`) and both Tab wrap directions. `Continue` is focused programmatically, not clicked (it's the submit button).

**Throwaway probe (written, run, deleted):** mounted the real `Footer` + real hook in Vitest and mirrored the final play 1:1 — **passed**. It also printed the real focus order, confirming the assumption the play rests on: `INPUT[firstName], INPUT[lastName], A[Privacy Policy], BUTTON[Cancel], BUTTON[Continue]` → first = firstName, last = Continue.

**(b) NEW `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeModal.test.tsx`** — 3 tests. A synthetic harness with a disabled control at *both* ends of the focus order (unfiltered, `first` would be "Disabled leading" and `last` "Disabled trailing", so neither wrap would fire). Third test covers the scroll lock restoring a *non-empty* prior value (`'scroll'`) — the half of lines 63-70 a story can't reach, since a story only ever sees `''` restored.
